summary: OpenAI launched Daybreak, a suite of cybersecurity tools including an updated Codex Security plugin, the full release of GPT-5.5-Cyber to trusted defenders, a Daybreak Cyber Partner Program, and the Patch the Planet open-source patching initiative.

mechanisms.reason: Codex Security is described as autonomously scanning and resolving hundreds of thousands of findings at scale without human review for most of them.
mechanisms.quote: Since launching Codex Security cloud in research preview in March, it has scanned over 30 million commits across more than 30,000 codebases; human reviewers have manually marked more than 70,000 findings as fixed, and over 500,000 findings have automatically been determined to be fixed.

mechanisms.reason: The scale of automated scanning across millions of commits and tens of thousands of codebases implies substantial aggregate inference volume for this security workflow.
mechanisms.quote: it has scanned over 30 million commits across more than 30,000 codebases

practices.reason: GPT-5.5-Cyber shows stated benchmark gains in vulnerability discovery, exploit generation and long-horizon analysis, but is only available to verified defenders in limited release.
practices.quote: On CyberGym, which measures whether an agent can reproduce known vulnerabilities in software environments, the updated GPT‑5.5‑Cyber reached 85.6% in single-model evaluations, compared with 81.8% for GPT‑5.5.

practices.reason: Named benchmarks (CyberGym, ExploitGym, SEC-bench Pro) with concrete pass rates give a reproducible way to measure a model's real-world vulnerability discovery and exploitation capability.
practices.quote: GPT‑5.5‑Cyber also outperformed GPT‑5.5 on two demanding real-world security benchmarks: 39.5% versus 25.95% on ExploitGym, which tests whether agents can turn known vulnerabilities into working exploits that achieve unauthorized code execution.

practices.reason: Teams adopting Codex Security would need to wire its scan outputs into existing vulnerability management systems via SARIF/CodeQL exports.
practices.quote: When Codex Security completes a scan, it can also export to an existing vulnerability management system or integrate into tools with SARIF files, CodeQL queries, and more.

notable_reason: Discloses concrete scale figures (30M commits scanned, 500K findings auto-resolved) and a new state-of-the-art cyber benchmark score, marking a substantive step in agentic vulnerability remediation rather than routine product marketing.
